Student.title: Student
Student.description: Represents a student in the college e-voting system.

id.description: Unique identifier for the student entity.

collegeId.description: The college-assigned identifier for the student.

collegeName.description: The name of the college the student attends.

course.description: The course the student is enrolled in.

year.description: The year the student is currently in (e.g., FY, SY, TY), if applicable.

hasVoted.description: Indicates whether the student has already voted.

Admin.title: Admin
Admin.description: Represents an administrator user who can manage candidates and voting results.

id.description: Unique identifier for the admin user.

Candidate.title: Candidate
Candidate.description: Represents a candidate for a specific position in the election.

position.description: The position the candidate is running for.

manifesto.description: A brief statement of the candidate's platform.

Vote.title: Vote
Vote.description: Represents a vote cast by a student for a candidate.

timestamp.description: Timestamp of when the vote was cast.

VotingResult.title: VotingResult
VotingResult.description: Stores the aggregated voting results for each candidate.

id.description: Unique identifier for the voting result.

voteCount.description: The number of votes received by the candidate.

ContactMessage.title: ContactMessage
ContactMessage.description: Represents a message submitted through the contact form.

name.description: The name of the person who submitted the message.

email.description: The email address of the person who submitted the message.

timestamp.description: Timestamp of when the message was sent.

Election.title: Election
Election.description: Represents a concluded and archived election event.

id.description: Unique identifier for the archived election.

name.description: A descriptive name for the election (e.g., 'Spring 2024 Election').

startDate.description: The start date and time of the election period.

endDate.description: The end date and time of the election period.

results.description: A snapshot of the candidates and their final vote counts.

totalVotes.description: The total number of votes cast in the election.

firestore.reasoning:
The Firestore structure is designed to support the CampusVote application, emphasizing security, scalability, and ease of maintenance. It leverages structural segregation to enforce consistent security rules across collections and authorization independence by denormalizing data to avoid complex `get()` calls in security rules. 

*   `/admins/{adminId}`: Stores admin user data. This is a private collection accessible only to admins, storing their authentication information.
*   `/students/{studentId}`: Stores student data.  The `studentId` becomes the document ID.  The `hasVoted` field indicates whether a student has voted, enforcing the single-vote requirement. Security rules will ensure that only authenticated students can access their own documents.
*   `/candidates/{candidateId}`: Stores candidate information. Accessible to both students (for viewing) and admins (for management). 
*   `/votes/{voteId}`: Stores individual vote records. Each document contains the `studentId` and `candidateId`.  Security rules will ensure that only authenticated students can create vote documents, and each student can only create one.
*   `/voting_results/{candidateId}`: Stores the aggregated vote counts for each candidate.  This collection is primarily managed by the system/admin.  The `candidateId` is also used as the document ID.
*   `/elections/{electionId}`: Stores archived data for completed elections. This is an admin-only collection used for historical records and auditing.

**Authorization Independence:**  The `students` collection includes the `hasVoted` field. This denormalization is critical. Without it, security rules would need to read the `votes` collection to determine if a student has already voted, which breaks atomic operations.

**QAPs (Rules are not Filters):**
*   The segregation of students, admins, candidates, votes, and voting results into separate collections ensures that list operations can be secured effectively.  For example, listing candidates is open to all authenticated users, whereas listing votes is restricted. The `hasVoted` flag on student records also helps prevent filtering votes based on user status.

**Invariants:**
*   The structure facilitates enforcing invariants such as single voting by storing the `hasVoted` status directly on the student document.  Timestamps on votes are automatically generated by the server, ensuring their integrity.
